blocks.text: Lortab addiction is a condition wherein a person makes use of the drug for prolonged period of time (may be several weeks or longer). If such thin happens, mental and physical dependence usually takes place and this is due to the sense of wellbeing attained by the user. When a person is addicted to Lortab, he will soon get multiple prescriptions from different doctors so as to support his uncontrolled cravings.

raw_html:
Lortab Addiction

What is it?

Lortab addiction is a condition wherein a person makes use of the drug for prolonged period of time (may be several weeks or longer). If such thin happens, mental and physical dependence usually takes place and this is due to the sense of wellbeing attained by the user. When a person is addicted to Lortab, he will soon get multiple prescriptions from different doctors so as to support his uncontrolled cravings.

This is difficult on the part of the user because Lortab is known to activate the reward system of the brain. The brain’s reward system with Lortab is so intense, focusing one’s attention around obtaining and taking the drug. Lortab has the ability to activate a person’s brain reward mechanism, thereby causing addiction in the process. This kind of drug also reduces one’s level of consciousness, making a person impaired and unable to make himself fully aware of what is going on around him.

Find A Drug Rehab

Lortab Description

Lortab is a kind of drug which is also known as hydrocodone, a medical prescription drug which is used for medical purposes. When taken, Lortab combines a painkiller (narcotic analgesic) and cough remedy with non-narcotic analgesic to treat moderate to severe pains. When induced, a person may experience a dangerous level of sedation, drowsiness and dizziness.

Withdrawal Symptoms

So, what happens when a person strives to stop using Lortab? If a regular user stops his consumption of the drug. He will automatically experience withdrawal symptoms within 6 to 12 hours. While these symptoms are not known to be life-threatening, the intensity one might feel may not be a good experience.

Find A Drug Rehab

Ideally, the intensity of withdrawal symptoms associated with Lortab depends of a person’s addiction to the drug. For an instance, the withdrawal symptoms may tend to increase and grow stronger for 24 to 72 hours and then decline in a gradual fashion for a period of 7 to 14 days. The withdrawal signs and symptoms include but are not limited to:

  • Intense cravings for the drug
  • Fever
  • Yawning
  • Sweating
  • Diarrhea
  • Runny nose
  • Eyes with dilated pupils
  • Muscle pains
  • Nausea or vomiting
  • Irritability
